pr_title: network: fixlets for manager state file

issue_context.title: timesyncd ignores DHCPv6-configured NTP server
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

253.6

### Used distribution

NixOS 23.05

### Linux kernel version used

6.1.47

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-timesync

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

`systemd-timesyncd` uses DHCPv6-configured NTP Server

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

`systemd-timesyncd` ignores DHCPv6-configured NTP Server

### Steps to reproduce the problem

_No response_

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

```sh
$ cat /etc/systemd/network/30-wan_hgw.network
[Match]
Name=wan_hgw

[Link]
RequiredForOnline=routable

[Network]
DHCP=yes
DHCPPrefixDelegation=true
IPForward=true
IPv6AcceptRA=true

[DHCPv4]
UseDNS=false
UseHostname=false
UseRoutes=false

[DHCPv6]
UseNTP=true
WithoutRA=solicit

[DHCPPrefixDelegation]
Announce=false
Assign=false
UplinkInterface=:self

[IPv6AcceptRA]
Token=::f21

$ cat /etc/systemd/networkd.conf
[Network]

$ cat /etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf
[Time]
NTP=

$ systemctl cat systemd-networkd
(snip)
Environment=SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug

$ systemctl cat systemd-timesyncd
(snip)
Environment=SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug

$ systemctl restart systemd-networkd
$ systemctl restart systemd-timesyncd

$ networkctl status wan_hgw
● 6: wan_hgw                                                                          
                     Link File: /etc/systemd/network/10-wan_hgw.link
                  Network File: /etc/systemd/network/30-wan_hgw.network
                         State: routable (configured)
                  Online state: online                                                
                          Type: ether
                          Path: pci-0000:01:00.3
                        Driver: igb
                        Vendor: Intel Corporation
                         Model: I350 Gigabit Network Connection
              Hardware Address: 2c:53:4a:07:f9:03 (Shenzhen Winyao Electronic Limited)
                           MTU: 1500 (min: 68, max: 9216)
                         QDisc: mq
  IPv6 Address Generation Mode: eui64
      Number of Queues (Tx/Rx): 8/8
              Auto negotiation: yes
                         Speed: 1Gbps
                        Duplex: full
                          Port: tp
                       Address: 192.168.18.41 (DHCP4 via 192.168.18.1)
                                2400:4051:c520:1e00::f21
                                fe80::2e53:4aff:fe07:f903
                       Gateway: fe80::2eff:65ff:fe38:7fc6
                           DNS: 2400:4051:c520:1e00:2eff:65ff:fe38:7fc6
                           NTP: 2404:1a8:1102::b         <- DHCPv6 issues NTP server addresses
                                2404:1a8:1102::a
                           SIP: 192.168.18.1
             Activation Policy: up
           Required For Online: yes
               DHCP4 Client ID: IAID:0x4fabaa6f/DUID
             DHCP6 Client IAID: 0x4fabaa6f
             DHCP6 Client DUID: DUID-EN/Vendor:0000ab111c741a944e2150b30000

$ timedatectl show-timesync --all
LinkNTPServers=                         <- No DHCP-configured NTP servers
SystemNTPServers=
RuntimeNTPServers=
FallbackNTPServers=0.nixos.pool.ntp.org 1.nixos.pool.ntp.org 2.nixos.pool.ntp.org 3.nixos.pool.ntp.org

ServerAddress=160.16.113.133
RootDistanceMaxUSec=5s

NTPMessage={ Leap=0, Version=4, Mode=4, Stratum=3, Precision=-25, RootDelay=2.334ms, RootDispersion=167us, Reference=761B6B93, OriginateTimestamp=Sun 2023-09-10 19:59:30 JST, ReceiveTimestamp=Sun 2023-09-10 19:59:30 JST, TransmitTimestamp=Sun 2023-09-10 19:59:30 JST, DestinationTimestamp=Sun 2023-09-10 19:59:30 JST, Ignored=no, PacketCount=2, Jitter=607us }
Frequency=2448872

$ journalctl -u systemd-networkd -u systemd-timesyncd -S "20:08:11"
```

review_comments:
It's apparently possible to stuff all sorts of binary data here:
```sh
-bash-5.2# networkctl status host0 --json=short | jq '.NTP[].Server'
"\\000\\000a"
"\\001\\002\\003"
"a\\010a"

-bash-5.2# grep NTP /run/systemd/netif/state 
NTP=\000\000a \001\002\003 a\010a
```
Looks like `dns_name_is_valid` is missing somewhere. (It's not necessarily related to this PR but I haven't seen this before).
